stories.original:
**Blik completes Poland's first agentic payment transaction**

*A live agentic transaction on domestic account-to-account rails extends the technology's footprint into a market with one of Europe's strongest national payment schemes.*

Blik has run its first agentic payment transaction, in which a user authorised an AI agent to search for a specific product and complete the purchase when it became available. The transaction moves agentic payments from the domain of card networks and global fintechs into a domestic account-to-account scheme with deep consumer penetration in Poland.

Agentic payments have gathered momentum across 2026, with Visa, Mastercard, ING, Credit Agricole and others completing pilot transactions. Most activity so far has centred on card-based rails or pan-European schemes. Blik's entry is different because it operates as a bank-owned mobile payment standard that accounts for more than 60% of Polish e-commerce transactions, giving it a direct path to consumer-scale adoption that card-network pilots have yet to demonstrate.

The transaction follows PPRO's partnership with Blik, announced in August, to develop agentic commerce capabilities for the Polish market. Whether domestic schemes can define their own agentic standards or will defer to global frameworks such as EMVCo's draft specification remains an open question, but Blik's move suggests at least some national schemes intend to compete rather than wait.

*Sources: [Blik records first agentic payment transaction](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48379/blik-records-first-agentic-payment-transaction?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

stories.original:
**EPC delays structured address migration beyond November deadline**

*All five SEPA payment scheme rulebooks are affected, extending the transition period for participants still using unstructured address formats beyond November 2026.*

The European Payments Council (EPC) has decided to delay the planned November 2026 end date for the unstructured address format across all five of its payment scheme rulebooks. The original deadline would have required all SEPA payment service providers to send and receive only structured address data in line with ISO 20022 messaging standards.

The decision mirrors the pattern set by Swift, which extended its own structured address migration deadline for cross-border ISO 20022 messages earlier this year. Both delays reflect persistent implementation challenges among smaller banks and payment service providers that have struggled to clean and restructure address data across legacy systems. The EPC has not yet confirmed a revised end date.

Participants that have already completed structured address compliance now face uncertainty about when the operational benefits of consistent data quality will materialise. Those still behind gain breathing room but not relief from the underlying obligation.

*Sources: [EPC delays address format migration timeline](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110873/epc-delays-address-format-migration-timeline?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

stories.original:
**EPC opens consultation on pan-European fraud data-sharing rulebook**

*Draft rules for the Fraud Information Distribution Arrangement would require payment providers across SEPA to exchange fraud intelligence under a common scheme, ahead of obligations in the Payment Services Regulation.*

The European Payments Council (EPC) has launched a public consultation on the proposed rulebook for its Fraud Information Distribution Arrangement (FRIDA) scheme, running from September 11 to December 10. The rulebook would govern how payment service providers exchange fraud data related to account-to-account payments across SEPA, establishing binding inter-provider rules, practices and standards for sharing suspicious activity indicators.

FRIDA is designed to anticipate the fraud data-sharing obligations set out in Articles 83 and 83a of the Payment Services Regulation, which is expected to take effect by mid-2028. The scheme envisages a federated model, connecting existing national fraud-sharing platforms through a central hub to create pan-European interoperability. The EPC issued a request for information in January to identify potential operators for that central platform and has been developing the rulebook through its FRIDA task force since 2025.

The three-month consultation marks the point at which the scheme moves from design to formal market scrutiny. For payment providers already operating national fraud-sharing arrangements, FRIDA will set the terms on which those systems must interoperate. For those without such arrangements, it will define the baseline they must meet.

*Sources: [Contributing to the future of payments in Europe](https://www.europeanpaymentscouncil.eu/) — European Payments Council*

stories.original:
**Mastercard launches Wallet Pay to drive interoperability across digital wallets**

*The product portfolio targets fragmentation in mobile wallet payments by standardising how Mastercard credentials work across wallet providers and merchants.*

Mastercard has launched Wallet Pay, a portfolio of products designed to support interoperability and reach across mobile wallet payments. The suite aims to standardise how Mastercard credentials are provisioned, authenticated and accepted across different wallet providers and merchant environments.

Digital wallet penetration in Europe continues to grow. UK mobile wallet registrations reached 65% of adults in the first half of 2025, and wallet-based payments are a core distribution channel for both card networks and emerging schemes such as Wero. The challenge for Mastercard is that wallet fragmentation, with different technical implementations across Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay and bank-owned wallets, creates friction for merchants and limits the network's ability to guarantee a consistent experience.

Wallet Pay positions Mastercard as the interoperability layer between wallet providers and merchants rather than a competitor to individual wallets. As wallet penetration deepens and new payment surfaces such as agentic commerce and in-car payments proliferate, that interoperability role is a strategic prize. Mastercard's approach parallels the network's broader strategy of embedding its infrastructure into new payment surfaces rather than owning the consumer-facing interface directly.

*Sources: [Mastercard to boost digital wallet uptake with Wallet Pay](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48376/mastercard-to-boost-digital-wallet-uptake-with-wallet-pay?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*
